doc.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: Basie recordings, John Hammond and losing the guitar chair
summary: He recorded once with Basie, was given notice in New York in favor of Freddie Green, and dropped guitar for fiddle.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: When did you do your first recordings?

Well I really didn’t get to record too many, I think one session with Count. And it was interesting, because after we got to New York, John Hammond you know he also told Count about me because he had some of his boys had been through Peoria, Illinois and I had been playing at a hotel there. And they checked on me playing fiddle and guitar, I played some of both. So I was playing guitar. And after we got to New York, John Hammond had promised some musicians there, you know, the first chance I get I’ll put you with one of my bands, you know. So I got my notice, I got my notice in New York. I was the number one guitarist in New York in Down Beat. I told a friend of mine, “Man, I got my notice.” He said, “Oh, man, ain’t nobody in New York could fill your spot.” I said, “Hell it ain’t” and I got my notice in my pocket. So that was Freddie Green I mean he stayed with the Count for forty years or something after that. But Freddie couldn’t — I was playing good guitar. After I left there, I said well I’m just going to try to play some fiddle. Because guitar was a hard instrument and it was a thing where after I played some guitar, with the chords, there was so much difference with the chords, and then when you play the fiddle you have to close back up because the positions is closer. It would take me a chorus before I could play in tune almost. So I just dropped the guitar and say I’m going to just play the fiddle. So that’s the reason I’m just mostly playing fiddle.
